items.failureBehavior: Report and discard only the invalid record; do not clamp or substitute its fields, and keep valid records within the 10-record bound.
items.text: At the new ApoMarioHighscore file parser and storeRun boundary, validate the complete record before appending it: score and survival time must be integers in [0,Integer.MAX_VALUE], name must be trimmed, non-blank, non-null, and at most 32 characters, and each line/record must be at most 256 bytes. Reject and report invalid records; retain valid records and evict records beyond the 10-record display capacity instead of rejecting a valid fitting record.

items.failureBehavior: On any write or replace failure, report it and leave the current validated list intact.
items.text: At persistAcrossRuns, serialize only the validated, at-most-10-record state, use a temporary sibling file followed by an atomic replace when supported, and report any failure while retaining the in-memory state for the current panel.
The donor stores names, times, and points in parallel lists; save() sends them to a network endpoint, while load() parses every third line as an integer point or time and otherwise stores a name.

items.failureBehavior: Reject and report the invalid record; preserve valid retained records and do not replace the rejected value with a guessed or clamped value.
items.text: ApoMarioHighscore's file-reading and storeRun operations must accept only complete records with a non-negative integer score, a non-negative integer survival duration, and a non-null, non-blank-after-trimming name of at most 32 characters; each input record must be limited to 256 bytes, and the retained leaderboard must be limited to 10 records by evicting the lowest-ranked entries after insertion. Invalid records must be rejected and reported, never substituted or clamped by the store operation.

items.failureBehavior: Report the write failure and leave the validated in-memory leaderboard available for the current view; do not discard the run.
items.text: persistAcrossRuns must write the validated bounded leaderboard to the supplied Path and preserve the in-memory record if the file cannot be written; persistence errors must be reported without dropping the newly recorded run.
